Most companies I've worked for have had a fairly formal disciplinary process--you don't get fired until after you've been written up and failed an improvement plan that you agreed to (in lieu of being fired immediately).

Layoffs have either had notification (if they trust you and would benefit from a transition/debriefing period) or been accompanied by severance packages. I.e., we'll see our side of the transaction (the paycheck) through for a couple more weeks but no longer require you to provide labor, effective immediately. I think there was one case where the guy got both notification and severance.
Don't burn any bridges when you leave, you may need to use them again.

The only time my workplace ever fired people short notice was when they did something criminally punishable. Even then, unless you were caught in the act, you were notified of the investigation ahead of time, so you had time to make plans before your ass was kicked out. I'm sure it happens, but no one I know has ever worked anywhere that does layoffs or firing due to downsizing or poor performance without giving notice.

Something no one is mentioning: Oregon is an "at-will" state... you can quit anytime without notice. It might be a dick move, but if you've been mistreated and you have no reliance on them for referrals, or something... walk the fuck out if you feel like it (just make sure you're not gonna need to come grovelling back to them).
